title: Discontinuation or downtitration of guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure after changes in kidney function
content:
by Carine E. Hamo, Nathalia Ladino, Yunan Zhao, Morgan E. Grams, Patrick B. Mark, Adam N. Berman, Amrita Mukhopadhyay, Samrachana Adhikari, Saul Blecker

Background

Initiation of guideline directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with heart failure and reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) can cause acute declines in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) that are often reversible and clinically inconsequential yet may prompt premature therapy discontinuation.

Objectives

We aimed to quantify the frequency and magnitude of eGFR decline following GDMT initiation and its association with discontinuation or downtitration in individuals with HFrEF.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective analysis of adults with HFrEF and baseline eGFR > 30 ml/min/1.73 m2 who received a new prescription for an angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, angiotensin receptor blocker, angiotensin receptor neprilysin inhibitor, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, or sodium glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor between 4/1/2021–6/30/2024 within a large, diverse health system. The primary exposure was change in eGFR measured between 1 week and 3 months after GDMT prescription, categorized as no change/improvement or declines of 0–10%, 10–20%, 20–30% or ≥30%. We performed logistic regression to determine the association between eGFR change and GDMT discontinuation or downtitration.

Results

Among 4,335 individuals (mean age 69.2 years, 31% female, 19% Black adults), 35% did not have follow-up measurement of kidney function. eGFR declines of 20–30% and ≥30% were associated with higher odds of GDMT discontinuation or downtitration compared with no change/improvement (OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.17–2.00; OR 3.36, 95% CI 2.55–4.42, respectively).

Conclusions

Declines in eGFR ≥ 20% following GDMT initiation are associated with higher odds of discontinuation or downtitration. These associations raise the possibility that GDMT may be discontinued or downtitrated in response to clinically expected (<30%) alterations in kidney function.
